10.1016_j.cej.2025.163584: Carbonaceous materials are considered promising electrode materials for H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis and wastewater treatment. However, the structural design and modification of effective carbonaceous electrodes for simultaneous H 2 O 2 formation and pollutant degradation remain challenging. Herein, a reticulated vitreous carbon (RVC) electrode with an intrinsic three-dimensional porous structure was fabricated. The functional groups, defects and air-liquid-solid triple-phase interfaces were further incorporated into RVC by facile HNO 3 oxidation (HNO 3 -RVC), which was identified via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and contact angle tests. Compared with its pristine counterpart, HNO 3 -RVC yielded 1.5 times the one-hour cumulative H 2 O 2 concentration and 1.8 times the current efficiency. Furthermore, HNO 3 -RVC exhibited a 2-fold increase in ciprofloxacin (CIP) removal due to the synergistic effect of fast electrosorption and degradation. The incorporated C-O-C/COOH and defects are proposed to provide active sites for H 2 O 2 formation, and triple phase interfaces could transfer both dissolved and gaseous oxygen for H 2 O 2 formation. Scavenging tests indicated that ·SO 4 - and 1 O 2 act as the dominant reactive species for CIP degradation. Toxicity experiments suggested that some degradation products may exhibit greater toxicity than the parent CIP does, while prolonging the treatment time could reduce the toxicity.
10.1016_j.cej.2025.169890: Calcium oxide (CaO)-based sorbents are the most widely used materials for cyclic CO 2 capture in Sorption-Enhanced Steam Reforming (SESR) processes due to their high capacity, low cost, and wide availability. A critical limitation to their application is the progressive loss of activity over repeated carbonation–calcination cycles, mainly from sintering and pore structure degradation. This study examines regeneration strategies designed to mitigate sorbent deactivation and enhance long-term stability in cyclic SESR for producing renewable hydrogen from biomass. Three regeneration approaches, i.e., Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA), Temperature Swing Adsorption (TSA), and combined Pressure-Temperature Swing Adsorption (PTSA), were evaluated over multiple cycles under varying operational conditions. Structural degradation of the sorbent, characterized by crystallite growth and reductions in surface area and pore volume, was found to be primarily driven by thermal cycling. Under isothermal conditions, PSA showed better stability and higher residual CO 2 capture capacity than TSA, maintaining high activity over a greater number of cycles. For PSA, varying carbonation pressure between 5 and 15 bar had a minor effect on sorbent activity. In contrast, increasing regeneration temperature by 25 °C reduced regeneration time by approximately 40 %. Additionally, introducing 2.5 vol% steam during regeneration reduced desorption time by 32 %, likely due to beneficial structural changes such as macropore enlargement that mitigated diffusion limitations. Higher steam concentrations (up to 22.6 vol%) did not produce further improvements. Since SESR inherently operates in steam-rich environments, utilizing steam during regeneration offers both performance and process integration advantages. Overall, optimizing regeneration temperature, pressure, and atmosphere can enhance the efficiency and durability of natural CaO-based sorbents in cyclic CO 2 capture systems for hydrogen production.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.121135: Polymeric membranes containing adsorbent nanomaterials are a promising strategy for wastewater treatments, but few studies address chemical and morphological modifications in the polymer and related them to the performance of the membrane in real effluent treatment. In this study, for the first time, three-dimensional adsorbents were applied in the removal of heavy metals from a real electroplating wastewater. The prepared membranes were made from polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and mesoporous carbon doped with nitrogen and sulfur (NS-MPC). NS-MPC exhibited a three-dimensional porous structure with a high surface area (960.0 m 2 .g ̶1 ) and a pore volume of 3.43 cm 3 . g−1 The presence of NS-MPC in membranes resulted in the formation of irregular surfaces, increased porosity, square roughness (126 nm), and reduced hydrophilicity (12.05 o ). SEM images revealed the expansion of the fibrillary porous sublayers, mainly for hPAN@NS-MPC-10. This membrane showed the highest porosity and the best adsorptive performance toward heavy metals. The hPAN@NS-MPC membrane was selective for the removal of Al, Cr, Cu, Fe, and Pb, to the detriment of Ni, Zn, and Mn ions, when the concentrated electroplating bath was treated. When the electroplating effluent was used, hPAN@NS-MPC was able to remove Al, Cr, Cu, Fe, Pb, Ni, Zn, and Mn, with removal percentage between 57.6-93.8%. The hPAN@NS-MPC-10 has a comparable removal capacity to other powdered adsorbents. The pseudo-second-order and the intraparticle diffusion kinetic models were found to be the most suitable, indicating that chemisorption governs the mechanism for copper uptake. The hPAN@NS-MPC-10 exhibited 85.5% of removal for copper in filtration assays. • NS-MPC increased surface roughness and porosity of the hPAN@NS-MPC membranes; • NS-MPC provided a tridimensional fibrillary porous sublayer improving metals removal; • hPAN@NS-MPC exhibited high removal for Cu, Ni, Fe from an electroplating effluent; • 85.5% removal for Cu was achieved in filtration assays; • The complexation between Cu and hPAN@NS-MPC is the main mechanism;
10.1021_acs.analchem.5c00321: Real time detection of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in deep brain regions is of great significance. Photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensors hold promise for real-time monitoring but low sensitivity due to the use of small electrode restrained its application. In this study, a miniaturized sensor that integrates organic photoelectrochemical transistors (OPECTs) with optical fiber (OF) microelectrodes was designed for the first time, which can amplify the small PEC signal into large channel current change. A conductive gold layer and cuprous oxide nanoparticles (Cu2O NPs) were sequentially deposited onto the OF, followed by a Nafion polymer coating to enhance anti-interference capabilities. Cu2O reacts with H2S to generate Cu2S. The resulting Cu2O/Cu2S heterojunction induces changes in the PEC signal and channel current. Compared to a conventional PEC system, the OPECT sensor has higher sensitivity and lower detection limit, enabling monitoring of H2S concentration fluctuations within the rat brain, which demonstrates the approach’s capability for highly sensitive in vivo biomarker detection.
